title: Jerome on Matthew 1:1
body: “The face of a man' (in Ezekiel's vision) signifies Matthew, who accordingly opens his Gospel with the human genealogy of Christ.”
author: Jerome, Ez, i. 5. Hier. Prolog. in Com. in Matt, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 1:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 1:1
body: “Do ye indeed remember the charge, which we lately made you, entreating you to hearken unto all the things that are said with all silence, and mystical quietness? For we are to-day to set foot within the holy vestibule, wherefore I have also put you in mind of the charge.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 2

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 1:17
body: “He hath divided all the generations into three portions, to indicate that not even when their form of government was changed did they become better, but alike under an aristocracy, and under a king, and under an oligarchy, they were in the same evil ways, and whether popular leaders, or priests, or kings controlled them, it was no advantage to them in the way of virtue.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 4

title: Augustine on Matthew 2:1
body: “After the miraculous Virgin-birth, a God-man having by Divine power proceeded from a virgin womb; in the obscure shelter of such a cradle, a narrow stall, wherein lay Infinite Majesty in a body more narrow, a God was suckled and suffered the wrapping of vile rags - amidst all this, on a sudden a new star shone in the sky upon the earth, and driving away the darkness of the world, changed night into day; that the day-star should not be hidden by the night.”
author: Augustine, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 2:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 2:1
body: “We have need of much wakefulness, and many prayers, that we may arrive at the interpretation of the passage now before us, and that we may learn who these wise men were, and whence they came, and how; and at whose persuasion, and what was the star. Or rather, if ye will, let us first bring forward what the enemies of the truth say.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 6

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 2:2
body: “How then saith Luke, that He was lying in the manger? Because at the birth indeed she presently laid Him there (for, as was not unlikely, in that large assemblage for the taxing, they could find no house; which Luke also signifies, by saying, "Because there was no room, she laid Him" there); but afterwards she took Him up, and held Him on her knees.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 8

title: Hilary of Poitiers on Matthew 3:1
body: “Or, he came to Judaea, desert by the absence of God, not of population, that the place of preaching might witness the few to whom the preaching was sent.”
author: Hilary of Poitiers, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 3:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 3:1
body: “How "in those days"? For not then, surely, when He was a child, and came to Nazareth, but thirty years after, John cometh; as Luke also testifies.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 10

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 3:7
body: “How then doth Christ say, that they did not believe John? Because this was not believing, to decline receiving Him whom he preached.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 11

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 4:1
body: “Then. When? After the descent of the Spirit, after the voice that was borne from above, and said, "This is My Beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased." And what was marvellous, it was of the Holy Spirit; for this, he here saith, led Him up.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 13

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 4:1
body: “Whoever thou art then that after thy baptism sufferest grievous trials, be not troubled thereat; for this thou receivedst arms, to fight, not to sit idle.”
author: John Chrysostom, Hom. 13, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 4:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 4:12
body: “Wherefore doth He depart? Again instructing us not to go to meet temptations, but to give place and withdraw ourselves.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 14

title: Augustine on Matthew 5:1
body: “Or He may be thought to have sought to shun the thickest crowd, and to have ascended the mountain that He might speak to His disciples alone.”
author: Augustine, de Cons. Evan., ii, 19, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 5:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 5:27
body: “Having now finished the former commandment, and having extended it unto the height of self-denial, He, advancing in course and order, proceeds accordingly unto the second, herein too obeying the law.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 17

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 5:38
body: “Seest thou that it was not of an eye that He was speaking before, when He made the law to pluck out the offending eye, but of him who by his friendship is harming us, and casting us into the gulf of destruction? For He who in this place uses so great strength of expression, and who, not even when another is plucking out your eye, permits you to strike out his; how should He have made it a law to strike out one's own?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 18

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 6:1
body: “He roots out in what remains the most tyrannical passion of all, the rage and madness with respect to vainglory, which springs up in them that do right. For at first He had not at all discoursed about it; it being indeed superfluous, before He had persuaded them to do any of the things which they ought, to teach in which way they should practise and pursue them.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 19

title: Augustine on Matthew 6:1
body: “How great strength the love of human glory has, none feels, but he who has proclaimed war against it. For though it is easy for any not to wish for praise when it is denied him, it is difficult not to be pleased with it when it is offered.”
author: Augustine, Prosper. Lib. Sentent. 318, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 6:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 6:24
body: “Seest thou how by degrees He withdraws us from the things that now are, and at greater length introduces what He hath to say, touching voluntary poverty, and casts down the dominion of covetousness?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 21

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 7:1
body: “What then? Ought we not to blame them that sin? Because Paul also saith this selfsame thing: or rather, there too it is Christ, speaking by Paul, and saying, "Why dost thou judge thy brother?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 23

title: Augustine on Matthew 7:1
body: “Since when these temporal things are provided beforehand against the future, it is uncertain with what purpose it is done, as it may be with a single or double mind, He opportunely subjoins, "Judge not.”
author: Augustine, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 7:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 7:21
body: “Wherefore said He not, "but he that doeth my will?" Because for the time it was a great gain for them to receive even this first; yea it was very great, considering their weakness.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 24

title: Jerome on Matthew 8:1
body: “After the preaching and teaching, is offered an occasion of working miracles, that by mighty works following, the preceding doctrine might be confirmed.”
author: Jerome, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 8:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 8:5
body: “The leper came unto Him "when He was come down from the mountain," but this centurion, "when He was entered into Capernaum." Wherefore then did neither the one nor the other go up into the mountain?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 26

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 8:14
body: “But Mark adds also, "immediately," meaning to declare the time as well; but this evangelist hath set down only the miracle, without signifying besides the time. And whereas the others say, that she that lay ill did also entreat Him, this too he hath passed over in silence.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 27

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 9:1
body: “By His own city here he means Capernaum. For that which gave Him birth was Bethlehem; that which brought Him up, Nazareth; that which had Him continually inhabiting it, Capernaum.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 29

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 9:1
body: “By "his own city" is here meant Capharnaum. For one town, to wit, Bethlehem, had received Him to be born there; another had brought Him up, to wit, Nazareth; and a third received Him to dwell there continually, namely, Capharnaum.”
author: John Chrysostom, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 9:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 9:9
body: “For when He had performed the miracle, He did not remain, lest, being in sight, He should kindle their jealousy the more; but He indulges them by retiring, and soothing their passion. This then let us also do, not encountering them that are plotting against us; let us rather soothe their wound, giving way and relaxing their vehemence.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 30

title: Bede on Matthew 10:1
body: “For the number twelve, which is made up of three into four, denotes that through the four quarters of the world they were to preach the faith of the holy Trinity.”
author: Bede, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 10:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 10:16
body: “Yea, and many advantages were hence secured; and first, that they learnt the power of His foreknowledge; secondly, that no one should suspect, that through weakness of their Master came these evils upon them; thirdly, that such as undergo these things should not be dismayed by their falling out unexpectedly, and against hope; fourthly, that they might not at the very time of the cross be troubled on hearing these things.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 33

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 10:23
body: “Having spoken of those fearful and horrible things, enough to melt very adamant, which after His cross, and resurrection, and assumption, were to befall them, He directs again His discourse to what was of more tranquil character, allowing those whom He is training to recover breath, and affording them full security. For He did not at all command them, when persecuted, to close with the enemy, but to fly.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 34

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 11:1
body: “That is, after He had sent them, He proceeded to withdraw Himself, to give them room and opportunity to do what He had enjoined. For while He was present and healing, no one would be willing to approach them.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 36

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 11:25
body: “Seest thou, how many ways He leads them on to the faith? First, by His praises of John. For by pointing to him as a great and marvellous one, He proved likewise all his sayings credible, whereby he used to draw them on to the knowledge of Him.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 38

title: Augustine on Matthew 12:1
body: “This which here follows is related both by Mark and Luke, without any question of discrepancy; indeed they do not say, "At that time," so that Matthew has here perhaps preserved the order of time, they that of their recollection; unless we take the words in a wider sense, "At that time," that is, the time in which these many and divers things were done, whence we may conceive that all these things happened after the death of John.”
author: Augustine, De Cons. Ev., ii, 34, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 12:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 12:1
body: “But Luke saith, "On a double Sabbath." Now what is a double Sabbath? When the cessation from toil is twofold, both that of the regular Sabbath, and that of another feast coming upon it.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 39

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 12:9
body: “Again He heals on a Sabbath day, vindicating what had been done by His disciples. And the other evangelists indeed say, that He "set" the man "in the midst," and asked them, "If it was lawful to do good on the Sabbath days.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 40

title: Augustine on Matthew 12:32
body: “This word must be supplied from the former clause in the verse, "Whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Man" (Matt.”
author: Augustine, Homilies on the Gospels

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 13:1
body: “When He had rebuked him that told Him of His mother and His brethren, He then did according to their request; He departed out of the house, having first corrected His brethren for their weak desire of vainglory; He then paid the honour due to His mother, as it is said, "The same day Jesus went forth out of the house, and not down by the sea aide.”
author: John Chrysostom, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 13:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 13:10
body: “We have good cause to admire the disciples, how, longing as they do to learn, they know when they ought to ask. For they do it not before all: and this Matthew shows by saying, "And they came." And, as to this assertion not being conjecture, Mark hath expressed it more distinctly, by saying, that "they came to Him privately." This then His brethren and His mother should also have done, and not have called Him out, and made a display.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 45

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 13:24
body: “What is the difference between this, and the parable before it? There He speaks of them that have not at all holden with Him, but have started aside, and have thrown away the seed; but here He means the societies of the heretics.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 46

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 14:2
body: “It is not without reason that the Evangelist here specifies the time, but that you may understand the pride and carelessness of the tyrant; inasmuch as he had not at the first made himself acquainted with the things concerning Christ, but now only after long time. Thus they, who in authority are fenced about with much pomp, learn these things slowly, because they do not much regard them.”
author: John Chrysostom, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 14:2 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 14:13
body: “See Him on every occasion "departing," For not by His appearance only, but by His actions He would have this confirmed, because He knew the devil's craft, and that he would leave nothing undone to destroy this doctrine.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 49

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 14:23
body: “For what purpose doth He go up into the mountain? To teach us, that loneliness and retirement is good, when we are to pray to God.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 50

title: Augustine on Matthew 15:1
body: “The Evangelist thus constructs the order of his narrative, "Then came unto him," that, as appeared in the passage over the lake, the order of the events that followed that might be shewn.”
author: Augustine, de Cons. Ev., ii, 49, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 15:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 15:21
body: “But Mark saith, that "He could not be hid," though He had entered into the house. And why did He go at all into these parts?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 52

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 16:1
body: “As the Lord sent the multitudes away after the miracle of the five loaves, so also now, not on foot, but by boat, that the multitudes may not follow Him; "And He sent away the multitude, and entered into a ship, and came into the coasts of Magedan.”
author: John Chrysostom, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 16:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: Basil the Great on Matthew 16:19
body: “Here we see "binding and loosing" passing from the Scriptural sense of declaring what acts are forbidden and committed (Matt.”
author: Basil the Great, Hexaemeron

title: Jerome on Matthew 17:2
body: “It is made a question how it could be after six days that He took them, when Luke says eight. The answer is easy, that here one reckoned only the intervening days, there the first and the last are also added.”
author: Jerome, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 17:2 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 17:10
body: “Not then from the Scriptures did they know this, but the Scribes used to explain themselves, and this saying was reported abroad amongst the ignorant people; as about Christ also.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 57

title: Jerome on Matthew 18:2
body: “The disciples seeing one piece of money paid both for Peter and the Lord, conceived from this equality of ransom that Peter was preferred before all the rest of the Apostles.”
author: Jerome, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 18:2 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 18:21
body: “Peter supposed he was saying something great, wherefore also as aiming at greatness he added, "Until seven times?" For this thing, saith he, which Thou hast commanded to do, how often shall I do?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 61

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 19:1
body: “Having constantly left Judæa on account of the envy of those men, now He frequents it from this time forth, because the passion was to be nigh at hand; He goeth not up, however, unto Jerusalem for a while, but "into the coasts of Judæa.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 62

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 19:2
body: “The Lord had before left Judaea because of their jealousy, but now He keeps Himself more to it, because His passion was near at hand. Yet does He not go up to Judaea itself, but into the borders of Judaea; whence it is said, "And it came to pass when Jesus had ended all these sayings, he departed from Galilee.”
author: John Chrysostom, Hom., lxii, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 19:2 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: Gregory on Matthew 20:1
body: “Or; The Master of the household, that is, our Maker, has a vineyard, that is, the Church universal, which has borne so many stocks, as many saints as it has put forth from righteous Abel to the very last saint who shall be born in the end of the world.”
author: Gregory, Hom. in Ev., xix, 1, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 20:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 20:17
body: “For since it was likely that they, because they were not willing this should come to pass, would forget it, He is continually putting them in remembrance, exercising their mind by the frequency with which He reminded them, and diminishing their pain.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 65

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 20:29
body: “See whence He passed unto Jerusalem, and where He abode before this, with regard to which it seems to me especially worthy of inquiry, wherefore He went not away even long before this from thence unto Galilee, but through Samaria. But this we will leave to them that are fond of learning.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 66

title: Origen on Matthew 21:2
body: “Whence Bethphage is interpreted, The house of the Shoulder; for the shoulder was the priest's portion in the Law. It follows, "Then Jesus sent two of his disciples.”
author: Origen, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 21:2 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 21:12
body: “This John likewise saith, but he in the beginning of his Gospel, this at the end. Whence it is probable this was done twice, and at different seasons.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 67

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 22:1
body: “Forasmuch as He had said, And it shall be given to a nation bringing forth the fruits thereof," He now proceeds to shew what nation that is.”
author: John Chrysostom, Hom. lxix, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 22:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 22:1
body: “Seest thou both in the former parable and in this the difference between the Son and the servants? Seest thou at once the great affinity between both parables, and the great difference also?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 69

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 22:15
body: “Then. When? When most of all they ought to have been moved to compunction, when they should have been amazed at His love to man, when they should have feared the things to come, when from the past they ought to have believed touching the future also.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 70

title: Origen on Matthew 23:1
body: “The disciples of Christ are better than the common herd; and you may find in the Church such as with more ardent affection come to the word of God; these are Christ's disciples, the rest are only His people. And sometimes He speaks to His disciples alone, sometimes to the multitudes and His disciples together, as here.”
author: Origen, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 23:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 23:1
body: “Then. When? When He had said these things, when He had stopped their mouths; when He had brought them that they should no more dare to tempt Him; when He had shown their state incurable.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 72

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 23:14
body: “After this, next He derides them for gluttony: and the grievous thing was, that not from rich men's goods, but from the poor they indulged their own belly, and aggravated their poverty, which they should have relieved. For neither did they merely eat, but devoured.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 73

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 24:1
body: “For inasmuch as He said, "Your house is left desolate," and had previously forewarned them of many grievous things; therefore the disciples having heard these things, as though marvelling at it, came unto Him, showing the beauty of the temple, and wondering, if so much beauty was to be destroyed, and materials so costly, and variety of workmanship past utterance; He no longer thenceforth talks to them of desolation merely, but foretells an entire destruction.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 75

title: Origen on Matthew 24:2
body: “Christ, when He had foretold all that should come upon Jerusalem, "went forth out of the temple," He, who while He was in it, had upheld the temple that it should not fall. And so each man, being the temple of God by reason of the Spirit of God dwelling in him, is himself the cause of his being deserted, that Christ should depart from him.”
author: Origen, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 24:2 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 24:16
body: “Having spoken of the ills that were to overtake the city, and of the trials of the apostles, and that they should remain unsubdued, and should overrun the whole world, He mentions again the Jews' calamities, showing that when the one should be glorious, having taught the whole world, the others should be in calamity.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 76

title: Hilary of Poitiers on Matthew 25:1
body: “Then," because all this discourse is concerning the great day of the Lord, concerning which He had been speaking before.”
author: Hilary of Poitiers, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 25:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 25:1
body: “These parables are like the former parable of the faithful servant, and of him that was ungrateful and devoured his Lord's goods. For there are four in all, in different ways admonishing us about the same things, I mean about diligence in almsgiving, and about helping our neighbor by all means which we are able to use, since it is not possible to be saved in another way.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 78

title: Hilary of Poitiers on Matthew 26:1
body: “After the discourse in which the Lord had declared that He should return in splendour, He announces to them His approaching Passion, that they might learn the close connection between the sacrament of the Cross, and the glory of eternity.”
author: Hilary of Poitiers, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 26:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 26:6
body: “This woman seems indeed to be one and the same with all the evangelists, yet she is not so; but though with the three she doth seem to me to be one and the same, yet not so with John, but another person, one much to be admired, the sister of Lazarus.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 80

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 26:17
body: “By the first day of the feast of unleavened bread, he means the day before that feast; for they are accustomed always to reckon the day from the evening, and he makes mention of this in which in the evening the passover must be killed; for on the fifth day of the week they came unto Him.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 81

title: Augustine on Matthew 27:1
body: “The Evangelist had above brought down his history, of what was done to the Lord as far as early morning; he then turned back to relate Peter's denial, after which he returned to the morning to continue the course of events,”
author: Augustine, de Cons. Ev., iii, 7, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 27:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 27:27
body: “As though on some signal the devil then was entering in triumph into all. For, be it that Jews pining with envy and jealousy were mad against Him, as to the soldiers, whence was it, and from what sort of cause?”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 87

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 27:45
body: “This is the sign which before He had promised to give them when they asked it, saying, "An evil and adulterous generation seeketh after a sign, and there shall no sign be given to it, but the sign of the prophet Jonas;" meaning His cross, and His death, His burial, and His resurrection.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 88

title: Bede on Matthew 28:1
body: “Otherwise; It may be understood that they began to come in the evening, but that it was the dawn of the first day of the week when they reached the sepulchre; that is, that they prepared the spices for anointing the Lord's body in the evening, but that they took them to the sepulchre in the morning. This has been so shortly described by Matthew, that it is not quite clear in his account, but the other Evangelists give the order more distinctly.”
author: Bede, Beda in loc, quoted in Aquinas, Catena Aurea on Matthew 28:1 (tr. J. H. Newman)

title: John Chrysostom on Matthew 28:11
body: “For the sake of these soldiers that earthquake took place, in order to dismay them, and that the testimony might come from them, which accordingly was the result. For the report was thus free from suspicion, as proceeding from the guards themselves.”
author: John Chrysostom, Homilies on Matthew, Homily 90
